title: LumenWare inference cost playtest summary
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight playtest summary for LumenWare (customer) showing an explicit before/after economics snapshot for their chat+search inference workload using Redwood Optimize recommendations. The goal is to align on likely monthly $ savings, main levers, rollout plan, and measurement hooks for a small canary rollout.

Executive summary (one line):
Applying Redwood Optimize recommendations (KV prefix cache + conservative quantization + guided batching) is estimated to reduce LumenWare hosted inference spend by ~42% (from $28.6k/mo to $16.5k/mo) for the modeled workload, with a 10–15% latency tail increase in some read-heavy flows unless we enable dynamic routing.

Context and customer profile:
- Product: LumenWare search + chat assistant embedded in help center (SaaS).
- Current deployment: Hosted API, mixed GPT-like open models (32-bit fp mixed), per-token billing with 10M tokens/day average (burst to 25M/day).
- Workload shape: 70% short chats (avg 120 tokens request + 40 tokens response), 30% long retrieval+summarization (avg 600 tokens request + 400 tokens response). Peak concurrency spikes at 420 RPS for short chat during US morning.
- Current monthly cost observed (billing export): $28,640 (model compute + networking + infra overhead tagged to hosted usage).

Assumptions used in model (explicit):
- Token accounting: billable token counts are measured as request+response tokens. We used customer-provided telemetry for avg tokens/day and distribution aggregated over Jan 2026.
- Baseline throughput: no prefix caching, default batching (server default small batch windows), full fp model variant.
- After-optimize targets: enable prefix/KV cache for repeated retrieval prompts (estimated 18% of total token load is cacheable), enable int8 quantization profile (conservative — forward-only quantize, not kv-cache quantize), tuning batching windows to 8–12ms target latency for medium priority tier.
- Hardware routing: assume requests remain on same hosted capacity class; no change in GPU class.
- Price per GPU token cost used is from Redwood internal catalog (anonymized) consistent with hosted pricing as of Feb 2026.

Modeled before/after snapshot (monthly) — summary table:
| Metric | Before Redwood Optimize | After Redwood Optimize (recommended) | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Billable tokens / month | 300,000,000 | 246,000,000 | 18% cache hit reduces tokens; batching reduces duplicate model invocations
| Effective model compute $ | $24,200 | $13,900 | quantization + batching savings on per-token compute
| Network + infra overhead $ | $3,100 | $2,600 | small reduction from fewer inflight requests
| Total monthly cost $ | $28,640 | $16,500 | ~42% reduction (rounded)

Key levers and estimated impact (how numbers were derived):
1) Prefix / KV caching (primary lever) — estimated 18% token reduction
   - Source: LumenWare telemetry shows ~22% of sessions repeat same retrieval prompt prefixes within 10 minutes. Conservatively modeled 18% effective cache hit after cache warming and TTL.
   - Operational note: needs cache key tuning and occasional TTL invalidation for dynamic content.

2) Conservative quantization (int8 forward pass) — ~30–35% compute cost reduction for quantized requests
   - Modeled as 0.9x latency change for short flows, 1.1x latency for certain long seqs due to quantization fallback paths. We assumed 60% of tokens can be served through quantized path.

3) Batching and adaptive windows — ~15% reduction in per-token compute accounting for throughput smoothing
   - Tuning batching windows from default 2–4ms to a 8–12ms target for medium-priority traffic increases batch occupancy at peak. We conservatively estimate 12% near-peak and 18% on mid-traffic; averaged to 15% in model.

4) Routing policy and fallback controls — supports reliability while keeping cost savings
   - Recommendation: route non-SLA debug/analytics calls to lower-cost model variants; keep canary traffic on optimized path and allow automatic fallback to baseline model on errors.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Quality regressions from quantization on abstractive summarization tasks.
  Mitigation: A/B eval set (50 prompt pairs) run pre-rollout; monitor Rouge/BLEU style proxies and human review for first 2k generated outputs. Gate quantization ramp on quality metric thresholds.

- Risk: Cache staleness causing incorrect retrievals for time-sensitive content.
  Mitigation: TTL policy, tagging of time-sensitive docs, and a cache invalidation webhook from LumenWare CMS.

- Risk: Tail latency regression for critical flows (search+highlight).
  Mitigation: Dynamic routing: pin high-priority requests to non-quantized path or to reserved capacity; allow fallback to baseline model with minimal user-visible impact.

Rollout plan (canary -> scale):
1) Day 0–3: Unit tests and offline evals — run full A/B quality checks with quantized models on stored prompt set (owner: Samira).
2) Day 4–7: Small canary (1% traffic) — enable KV cache + batching for non-critical routes, collect cost telemetry and errors. Accept threshold: no more than 2% relative drop in quality proxy metrics, <0.5% error rate increase. (owner: Priya + site reliability).
3) Week 2: Expand to 10% traffic if canary passes — measure effective token reduction vs expected. Increase batch window incrementally to target occupancy.
4) Week 3–4: 50% traffic if metrics good; finalize SLO adjustments and fallbacks.
5) Month 2: Full rollout contingent on cost/quality objectives.

Measurement plan and KPIs to validate savings:
- Primary KPI: monthly billed compute cost (direct comparison to baseline month) — expected target $16.5k ±10%.
- Secondary KPIs: billable tokens/month, 95th and 99th latency percentiles per route, quality proxy score delta, cache hit rate.
- Instrumentation: use per-route token-level analytics in Redwood Console (enable token tagging for canary cohort), export daily roll-up to LumenWare S3 for reconciliation.

Quick action items (next 7 days):
- [ ] Confirm TTL and invalidation hooks with LumenWare CMS (Diego)
- [ ] Push quantized model variant to canary namespace and run offline evals (Samira)
- [ ] Enable KV cache with conservative TTL=5m for help-center index (Avery)
- [ ] Create Jira tasks for routing policy changes and fallback rules (Priya)

Open questions / items to resolve:
- How sensitive are LumenWare users to 95th/99th tail latency changes for the long summarization flows? We need product input (PM) to set acceptable latency delta.
- Are there any compliance/PII rules that prevent caching certain query types? Need a list from customer.

Appendix: short calculation notes (compressed):
- Baseline tokens/month used: 300M (customer billing exports)
- Modeled cache hit: 18% -> tokens after cache = 246M
- Effective per-token compute $ reduction from quantization + batching = approx 43% overall on the reduced token base -> (0.57 * 246M tokens) equivalent baseline compute cost mapping to $13.9k
- Numbers rounded to nearest hundred for presentation.

If this summary looks reasonable I will convert the model into a small spreadsheet (sheet) with daily token traces, sensitivity sliders (cache hit, quantization coverage, batching occupancy) and publish for LumenWare stakeholders.

Notes to self: keep filename short when moving to final: lumenware-cost-playtest-v1.json
